lessons.c:
In online mode TwinCAT shows live variable values beside your code. Log in to the PLC, start it, and watch signals change in real time.

You can write test values, but be careful on a real machine: forcing outputs can cause movement.
lessons.x: You see bSensor turn TRUE as a box passes, and watch bDiverter follow.
lessons.ex: Log in to a simulated PLC and watch a counter change.
q: Values update as the PLC runs.

Login connects the editor to the target.
Find why logic is not working
You can see actual signal states.
TwinCAT overlays them in the editor.

lessons.c:
A watch window lists chosen variables with live values in one place. Add variables, expand structures, and write test values to check behaviour.

It is ideal when the variables you care about live in different programs.
lessons.x: Watch bStart, nStep and bMotor together to see why a sequence stalls.
lessons.ex: Create a watch list for a motor and its fault flags.

lessons.c:
A breakpoint pauses the PLC at a chosen line so you can step through the code and inspect values. You can step over, into and out of blocks.

Warning: halting the PLC on a real machine freezes outputs, so use breakpoints on simulators or when it is safe.
lessons.x: You set a breakpoint on the diverter line to see the values just before it fires.
lessons.ex: Explain why a breakpoint on a moving conveyor could be risky.

lessons.c: Frequent bugs are using = instead of :=, a missing END_IF, uninitialised variables, INT overflow, writing one output from two places, endless loops and forgetting edge detection.
lessons.x: Two programs both write bMotor, so it flips back and forth every scan.
lessons.ex: Review a program for outputs written in more than one place.
q: Writing one output from two places:

lessons.c: Work methodically: reproduce the fault, check inputs, then logic, then outputs. Change one thing at a time, read the error list and logger, and compare with a known good version.
lessons.x: The conveyor will not start: you check the start input, the interlocks, then the output.
lessons.ex: Write a four-step troubleshooting checklist for a motor that will not run.
